title: The State of AI Powered Search and Retrieval — Frank Liu, MongoDB (prev Voyage AI)
talk_summary: Frank Liu explains AI-powered search/retrieval: embeddings/RAG, reranking, structured filters, query decomposition, and future multimodal/instruction-tuned/agent-native databases. The practical lessons are to evaluate retrieval components per domain and combine embeddings with structured metadata and agentic query expansion rather than relying on embeddings alone.

takeaways.what_they_do: In RAG/search, combine embedding similarity with structured metadata filters such as state, official status, or document details inside the vector store or after retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to have a lot of that structured data that's a part of it

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue no single embedding model or LLM is best; teams should run evaluations for their specific application/domain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is no onesizefitsall embedding model. There's no oneizefits-all LLM. Always do evaluations

takeaways.what_they_do: An LLM decomposes a broad query into multiple subqueries, sends them to retrieval separately, then combines results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your LM could decompose that into Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 earnings and then send that as four separate queries

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a classic RAG plus re-ranking pipeline: retrieve candidate documents by embedding, then rerank them before giving to the LLM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You do this is a classic rag uh plus re-ranking approach.
